introduction: The period from 1206 AD to 1526 AD is known as the 'Delhi Sultanate' era, during which five successive Muslim dynasties ruled over Northern India. After the death of Muhammad Ghori, his slave Qutb-ud-din Aibak laid the foundation of this empire, which lasted until the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

core_concepts.title: The 5 Dynasties (Chronology)
core_concepts.description: Five dynasties ruled the Sultanate in this order: 1. Slave Dynasty (1206-1290), 2. Khalji Dynasty (1290-1320), 3. Tughlaq Dynasty (1320-1414), 4. Sayyid Dynasty (1414-1451), 5. Lodi Dynasty (1451-1526).

core_concepts.title: Slave Dynasty (Mamluk Dynasty)
core_concepts.description: Founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak. Its most prominent rulers were Iltutmish and Balban. Iltutmish is considered the 'real founder' of the Delhi Sultanate.

core_concepts.title: Razia Sultana
core_concepts.description: The daughter of Iltutmish, Razia Sultana (1236-1240) was the first and only Muslim woman ruler to sit on the throne of Delhi.

core_concepts.title: Khalji Dynasty
core_concepts.description: Founded by Jalaluddin Khalji, but Alauddin Khalji was its most powerful ruler, expanding the Sultanate deep into South India.

core_concepts.title: Lodi Dynasty and the End of the Sultanate
core_concepts.description: The Lodi dynasty was the last ruling family (they were Afghans, not Turks). In 1526, Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat, laying the foundation of the Mughal Empire.

important_entities.name: Qutb-ud-din Aibak
important_entities.significance: Known as 'Lakh Bakhsh' (giver of lakhs) for his generosity. He started the construction of the Qutb Minar.

important_entities.name: Iltutmish
important_entities.significance: Shifted the capital from Lahore to Delhi and introduced Arabic coinage (the silver 'Tanka' and copper 'Jital').

important_entities.name: Ibrahim Lodi
important_entities.significance: The only Sultan of Delhi to be killed on the battlefield (at Panipat).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aibak was the founder, but he never took the title of 'Sultan' and ruled from Lahore. Iltutmish took the title of Sultan and made Delhi the capital, hence he is the 'real' founder.
Calling it the Slave Dynasty is historically inaccurate as only 3 rulers (Aibak, Iltutmish, Balban) were initially slaves. Modern historians prefer the term 'Mamluk Dynasty'.

exam_strategy_tips: The correct chronological order of the five dynasties is one of the most frequently asked questions.
Remember the longest-ruling dynasty (Tughlaq - 94 years) and the shortest-ruling dynasty (Khalji - 30 years).
